questions.concept: Heading equal to default font size
questions.question: The default HTML font size is 16 px. Which heading tag has a default size equal to this value?
questions.explanation: Default sizes are h1 32 px, h2 24 px, h3 18.72 px, h4 16 px, h5 13.28 px and h6 12 px, so <h4> matches 16 px.

questions.concept: Handling EOFError when loading all records
questions.question: A binary file holds several records written with repeated pickle.dump() calls. When pickle.load() is called in a loop to read all of them, which exception signals that no records are left?
questions.explanation: Reading past the last pickled object raises EOFError, which is handled to stop the read loop cleanly.

questions.concept: Full form of R in RFID
questions.question: In RFID, used for identifying devices in IoT, what does the letter R stand for?
questions.explanation: RFID stands for Radio Frequency Identification.

questions.question: How many hosts can be configured using the subnet mask 255.255.255.128?
questions.explanation: 128 leaves 7 host bits: 2^7 - 2 = 126 usable hosts (network and broadcast addresses excluded).

questions.question: Who is called the father of theoretical computer science?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing, inventor of the Turing machine, is called the father of theoretical computer science.

questions.question: Testing of an individual module, usually carried out by the programmers themselves, is:
questions.explanation: Unit testing tests an individual module and is done by programmers; integration testing combines modules and is done by testers.

questions.question: Who introduced the term Internet of Things in 1999?
questions.explanation: Kevin Ashton introduced IoT in 1999. Vint Cerf is the father of the Internet, McCarthy of AI, and Haartsen invented Bluetooth.

questions.concept: Infinite loop when condition never becomes False
questions.question:
What happens when the following code runs?
i = 1
while i < 5:
    print(i)

options.D: It prints 1 repeatedly in an infinite loop

questions.explanation: i is never changed inside the loop, so the condition i < 5 stays True forever and the loop never ends.

questions.question: Which self-balanced search tree is described as a 'fat tree' because each node holds multiple keys and has more than two children?
questions.explanation: A B-Tree node stores multiple keys and has more than two children. AVL and Red-Black trees are binary search trees.

questions.question: To defeat a keylogger that records which key positions are pressed, which input method is safer, and why?

options.A: Online virtual keyboard, because its key layout is randomized
options.B: Physical keyboard, because keystrokes are hardware encrypted
options.C: On-screen keyboard, because its key layout is randomized
options.D: On-screen keyboard, because it uses a fixed QWERTY layout

questions.explanation: The on-screen keyboard uses a fixed QWERTY layout, while an online virtual keyboard randomizes the key layout, making recorded positions useless to a keylogger.

questions.question: In C++, constants are also called:
questions.explanation: Fixed values written directly in a program, such as 10 or 'a', are constants, also known as literals.

questions.question: Which CPU scheduling algorithm exists in both preemptive and non-preemptive versions?
questions.explanation: Priority scheduling has both forms. FCFS is only non-preemptive, while Round Robin and SRTF are preemptive.

questions.concept: Ada supports classes but not polymorphism
questions.question: Which language supports classes but does not support polymorphism?
questions.explanation: Ada is the language that supports classes without supporting polymorphism; C++, Java and Smalltalk all support polymorphism.

questions.question: The payment app abbreviation BHIM stands for:
questions.explanation: BHIM is Bharat Interface for Money.

questions.question: Injection vulnerabilities typically target which of the following?

options.A: Wi-Fi passwords, WPA2 keys and routers
options.B: SQL queries, XML parsers and program arguments
options.C: Printer spools, cookies and virus definition files
options.D: Boot sectors, RAM and BIOS chips

questions.explanation: Injection vulnerabilities target SQL, XML parsers and program arguments by inserting malicious input.

questions.concept: SQL developed at IBM by Chamberlin and Boyce
questions.question: SQL was initially developed at IBM by which two people?

options.A: Raymond F. Boyce and E. F. Codd
options.B: Donald D. Chamberlin and Raymond F. Boyce
options.C: E. F. Codd and Charles Bachman
options.D: Charles Bachman and Donald D. Chamberlin

questions.explanation: SQL was developed at IBM by Donald D. Chamberlin and Raymond F. Boyce; Codd proposed the relational model and Bachman built IDS.

questions.question: Which of the following are listed as examples of software quality metrics? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: LOC, Function Points and Cyclomatic Complexity are the quality metrics given as examples. SWOT analysis is a planning technique used in requirement analysis, not a metric.

questions.concept: File or table as group of records
questions.question: In the database hierarchy, what is a group of related records called?
questions.explanation: Fields group into records, records group into files or tables, and files group into a database.

questions.concept: Building order of symbol, alphabet, word, language
questions.question: Which sequence correctly orders the basic automata terms from the smallest unit to the largest collection?
questions.explanation: A symbol is a character, an alphabet is a set of symbols, a word is built from the alphabet and a language is a set of words.

questions.concept: Virtual memory implemented via demand paging
questions.question: Virtual memory is commonly implemented using which technique?
questions.explanation: Virtual memory is implemented via demand paging, with pages swapped in and out of secondary memory as needed.

questions.question: Which statement about pseudocode is correct?

options.A: It is translated directly into machine code by the compiler
options.B: It must follow the exact syntax of a programming language
options.C: It is a non-formal language for human reading and cannot be executed directly by a computer
options.D: It represents steps using standard shapes connected by arrows

questions.explanation: Pseudocode is an informal description for humans and cannot be run directly. Shapes and arrows describe a flowchart.

questions.question: Which shortest path algorithm is cited as being used in currency conversion?
questions.explanation: Bellman-Ford handles negative weight edges and is used in currency conversion. Prim's and Kruskal's are MST algorithms.

questions.concept: CREATE INDEX creates a search key
questions.question: Which SQL command creates a search key on a table to speed up data lookup?
questions.explanation: CREATE INDEX creates an index (search key); DROP INDEX deletes it.

questions.concept: Class and default mask from an address
questions.question: The IPv4 address 150.10.20.30 belongs to which class, and what is its default subnet mask?
questions.explanation: First octet 150 lies in 128-191, so it is Class B with default mask 255.255.0.0.

questions.question: When the cache is full, the LRU replacement policy discards:

options.A: The least frequently used data first
options.B: The data that entered the cache first
options.C: The most recently used data first
options.D: The least recently used data first

questions.explanation: LRU (Least Recently Used) removes the item unused for the longest time. Removing the oldest entry is FIFO, and the least frequently used is LFU.
